note: The two sets are nearly identical in content and share the same defects: both duplicate the 250-louver, 32-rod and 15–30C facts under two names, and both assert unsupported connections (idler pulley–Kevlar string, Kevlar string–tension spring) whose quotes are only diagram labels. Set A adds one further correct claim that Set B omits — that rotational movement is transferred via Kevlar strings to each pulley — supported verbatim by the text. Both also leave out other stated design parameters (cross ventilation, privacy) and the hysteresis/anti-cycling function. On balance A is marginally better for the extra supported claim.
remarks: Both sets treat diagram callout labels (IDLER PULLEY, KEVLAR STRING, TENSION SPRING, etc.) as evidence of connections between parts; the labels only name parts, so those two connection claims are unsupported in both sets. Both miss the other two design parameters (allow cross ventilation, maintain privacy), the hysteresis function of preventing continuous open/close cycles, and the purpose of accurate hole placement (limiting binding and friction). Set A's louver quote reads 'cutting of each of the 250 louvers' where the text says 'cutting each of the 250 louvers' — a trivial quote slip.
